chunks: And Ḥarīz narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman who performed three circuits of tawaf or less than that, then saw blood. He said: “She should preserve her place, and when she becomes pure, she should perform tawaf from there and count what has already passed.”
And al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams عليهما السلام:

key_terms.اعْتَدَّتْ: she counts or considers as valid
key_terms.تَحْفَظُ: she keeps track of or preserves
key_terms.دَمًا: blood, here referring to menstrual bleeding
key_terms.طَافَتْ: performed tawaf, meaning she circumambulated the Kaʿbah
key_terms.مَا مَضَى: what has already passed or been completed
key_terms.مَكَانَهَا: her place or stopping point in the tawaf

ai.seo_question: What should a woman do if menstruation begins during tawaf before she completes it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a woman whose tawaf is interrupted by menstrual bleeding. She marks the point she reached, and after becoming pure, she resumes from that place and counts the rounds already completed. A second transmission reports the same ruling from one of the two Imams عليهما السلام.
